subject: Whether the 2023-2025 memory recovery should be represented as an AI-caused industry-wide upswing or as conventional DRAM/NAND cycle recovery plus AI-driven HBM and enterprise-product mix overlays

supported.finding: The already-grounded combined-recovery trajectory preserves a 2022 Micron DRAM/NAND wafer-start reduction and subsequent supplier production-cut expectations before later conventional PC/mobile demand improvement became known.
supported.meaning: Conventional DRAM/NAND entered the later recovery with a documented non-AI supply-correction mechanism already in motion; a broad 2024 recovery therefore cannot be attributed to AI merely because AI products were strong at the same time.

supported.finding: The combined-recovery trajectory records Samsung's Q3 2023 PC/mobile memory-demand improvement as a later-known Reality milestone, with no-lookahead replay preserving its November 2023 known time.
supported.meaning: At least one conventional end-market recovery signal existed before the 2024 HBM/product-mix bridge assembled here. This does not prove a full conventional recovery, but it rejects a chronology in which all recovery begins with 2024 AI demand.

supported.finding: In January 2024 TrendForce framed persistence of the broad DRAM/NAND price rally as depending on continued supplier control of capacity utilization.
supported.meaning: Contemporaneous market framing still treated supply discipline/utilization as material to broad memory pricing after the downturn; this is distinct from AI-specific demand strength and remains an expectation rather than a realized causal coefficient.

supported.finding: In April 2024 SK hynix explicitly described AI-memory demand as continuing to rise while separately expecting conventional DRAM to begin recovering in the second half.
supported.meaning: The supplier itself did not describe AI memory and conventional DRAM as one homogeneous demand trajectory. Product-line decomposition is therefore more faithful than an aggregate 'AI recovery' label.

supported.finding: By June 2024 TrendForce described the observed first-half NAND price rebound as occurring while manufacturers kept production in check.
supported.meaning: NAND provides a direct broad-recovery example in which supply restraint is part of the observed rebound mechanism; this cannot be replaced by an HBM narrative because HBM is a DRAM product family and the packet does not establish an AI-only NAND causal share.

supported.finding: The existing HBM3E trajectory separately preserves 2024 HBM3E production, sampling and customer-supply states and their contemporaneous Judgments without merging those states into conventional DRAM.
supported.meaning: AI demand is strongly material to HBM/high-value memory mix and should remain visible as a separate product trajectory rather than being minimized simply because conventional recovery also had supply/inventory mechanics.

supported.finding: Existing enterprise-SSD/QLC research has multiple 2024 commercialization and qualification signals around data-center/AI storage while explicitly leaving AI-only industry demand magnitude unresolved.
supported.meaning: AI is also a credible high-value NAND/SSD mix overlay, but supplier revenue, qualification and vendor shipment signals do not establish how much of total NAND recovery was caused by AI.

supported.finding: By October 2024 TrendForce's Q4 outlook explicitly separated weak conventional-DRAM price momentum from an uplift to overall DRAM pricing associated with the rising HBM share.
supported.meaning: Aggregate DRAM metrics can move differently from conventional DRAM because product mix changes. An industry-level price or revenue upswing therefore cannot be read as a homogeneous demand recovery without product decomposition.

not_established: The packet does not quantify the percentage of the 2024 memory recovery caused by AI, supplier cuts, inventory normalization or conventional end-market demand.
The packet does not establish that AI demand was irrelevant; HBM and enterprise/data-center storage evidence materially supports an AI-driven high-value mix overlay.
The January capacity-utilization condition is not a realized full-year supplier-utilization measurement.
The April conventional-DRAM second-half recovery statement is a supplier outlook, not a realized industry Outcome.
The October conventional-DRAM/HBM price decomposition is a forecast and must not be backdated into first-half 2024 replay.
The enterprise-SSD evidence does not establish an industry-wide AI-only NAND demand quantity or causal fraction.
No cross-product substitution coefficient between HBM capacity allocation and conventional DRAM bit supply is established here.

point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2023_10_31: A researcher can observe prior supplier production cuts and some conventional PC/mobile recovery signals from the existing combined-recovery trajectory, but cannot yet use the later January/April/June/October 2024 bridge or later HBM mix decomposition.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2024_01_20: The broad memory-price rally is contemporaneously framed as depending on continued capacity-utilization control. This strengthens the non-AI conventional-cycle explanation but still provides no AI causal share.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2024_04_26: SK hynix now explicitly separates continuing AI-memory demand growth from an expected second-half conventional-DRAM recovery, while the independent HBM3E trajectory already exposes product-specific AI-memory states.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2024_06_29: TrendForce additionally describes a first-half NAND price rebound associated with restrained production. The conventional-cycle explanation now spans both DRAM/NAND supply correction while AI strength remains separately visible in HBM and enterprise storage.
point_in_time_interpretation.as_of_2024_10_10: A later TrendForce forecast explicitly shows conventional DRAM and HBM mix diverging in price contribution. Aggregate DRAM should now be interpreted with product-mix decomposition rather than as one homogeneous recovery series.

counterfactual_evaluation.reason_ai_only: The evidence preserves supply cuts and conventional-demand recovery before the 2024 AI bridge, a broad price-rally condition tied to capacity utilization, a NAND rebound associated with restrained production, and later explicit divergence between conventional DRAM and HBM mix. AI is clearly material in HBM/high-value enterprise products but is not demonstrated as the sole cause of the broad DRAM/NAND recovery.
counterfactual_evaluation.reason_decomposition: This representation fits the source scopes and chronology without forcing incomparable product lines into one causal scalar: conventional DRAM/NAND preserve cut/inventory/recovery dynamics, HBM preserves a distinct AI-memory trajectory, and enterprise SSD/QLC preserves a separate AI/data-center commercialization overlay.
counterfactual_evaluation.preferred_research_representation: Represent recovery as at least three parallel state families: conventional DRAM/NAND cycle state, HBM/AI product-mix state, and enterprise-SSD/data-center storage state. Aggregate price/revenue measures may be composed only with explicit mix semantics and should not inherit an unmeasured AI causal share.

assessment.representation_decision: Keep the cross-product causal synthesis in the CAP-0006 research-only lane. Reuse the existing typed supplier-cut/recovery and HBM trajectories as authoritative for their own scoped states rather than creating a new aggregate AI-recovery truth object.
assessment.canonical_projection_decision: No new canonical causal predicate is needed. The January and October methodological-primary forecasts are potential CAP-0004 Judgment candidates if later product use requires typed replay; the June NAND rebound is a potential source-scoped Reality candidate only if an existing predicate can represent the observation without inventing a causal coefficient. Existing typed HBM and supplier-cut trajectories remain separate authority.
assessment.outcome_for_ms0120: MS-0120 is supported. The 2024 memory recovery should not be summarized as simply 'caused by AI.' Conventional DRAM/NAND recovery retained ordinary cycle mechanics including production cuts, inventory normalization and conventional demand improvement, while AI materially strengthened HBM and high-value enterprise-product mix. The relative causal weights remain unresolved.

stop_rule.closed_surface: Do not spend additional search budget on generic articles debating whether AI did or did not cause the memory recovery. The useful distinction is now product-line and state-variable decomposition, not another narrative vote.
reopen_when: A methodological-primary source quantifies comparable conventional-DRAM, HBM and NAND/enterprise-SSD bit, revenue or price-mix contributions on the same period and denominator.
A primary or methodological-primary source directly quantifies the contribution of AI workloads to total DRAM or NAND demand rather than only HBM/eSSD product growth.
Realized Q4 2024 conventional-DRAM versus HBM price/mix data allow the October forecast to be evaluated as an Outcome.
Comparable capacity-allocation data quantify whether HBM production materially constrained conventional DRAM bit supply.

next_research_direction.rationale: The AI-versus-conventional recovery decomposition is now sufficiently grounded. The next high-value counterfactual tests whether 2016-2018 NAND tightening is better explained by temporary 2D-to-3D transition loss versus demand/bit-growth dynamics.
